newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Mabuhay Vinyl proposes new IPO price.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Mabuhay Vinyl proposes new IPO price.

text.p: Chemical producer Mabuhay Vinyl Corp said on Tuesday it has revised the price range for its initial public offering to a range of between 2.23 and 2.97 pesos to reflect the lower projected 1997 earnings.
Earlier, the firm proposed to sell to the public at the price of 2.38 to 3.18 pesos, or at 12 to 16 times projected eartnings for 1997. The SEC had approved the IPO earlier this month.
The firm said in documents submitted to the SEC that the revised price range reflected the same price-earnings multiple of 12 to 16 times.

It had changed its forecast for 1997 to take into account the lower selling price of polyviynyl chloride (PVC) resin. Net profits for 1997 is projected to be at 122.083 million pesos, 26 percent higher than the 1996 estimate of 97.179 million pesos, the firm said.

Mabuhay Vinyl, a major producer of PVC resin, plans to offer 223.187 million shares to the public. It plans to use the proceeds of the IPO to fund its 49 percent equity investment in Philippine Resins Industries Inc, a 70,000-tonne PVC resin plant in Bataan near Manila in a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corp and Tosoh Corp and Bank of the Philippine Islands.

The major stockholders of Mabuhay Vinyl are the Bank of the Philippine Islands, with 34.08 percent; Maria Christina Chemicals Industries Corp, 29.96 percent; Asian Investment Co Ltd, 12.83; Eastide Philippines Co Inc, 9.54 percent; and Mitsubishi Corp, 3.35 percent.
BPI Capital Corp is lead underwriter of the offer.
